summary: Session 1 of 4 (Cross-platform schema applicator). Replaces the per-entity `Apply-{Entity}Schema.ps1` PowerShell post-process with a cross-platform .NET 10 console app `Dabbler.SchemaApplicator` plus an xUnit test suite that asserts byte-identical output against the committed PowerShell baseline (both as a string and as raw UTF-8 bytes - catches encoding regressions). 7/7 tests pass: idempotency on populated SupplierList/Detail.razor, fresh-template input -> committed PowerShell output (string + bytes), omitted-primary-key default to Id, unknown-type hand-edit placeholder, no-matching-properties empty state, and humanize+kebab handling on a compound name. CLI smoke against a tmp copy of the live Supplier files confirmed SHA-256 unchanged. Updated crud-page-template.md and crud-service-template.md to reference the new applicator and mark Apply-{Entity}Schema.ps1 deprecated. 2 cross-provider verification rounds via gpt-5-4: Round 1 ISSUES_FOUND (Major completeness - crud-service-template.md only had a cross-link, not its own deprecation note); Round 2 VERIFIED after adding a Related Tooling section. PowerShell scripts remain in place for backwards compatibility. SupplierScaffoldingExtensions.cs wrong-convention fix is Session 2's scope, not touched here.

reason.specifics: Session 2 (dabbler-crud-slice wrapper command) is mechanical orchestration and convention-based code generation - child-process invocation of dotnet new templates plus emitting a fixed scaffolding-extension shape. Routed Gemini Pro analysis confirms the cheapest capable choice is Sonnet 4.6 @ medium; Opus's reasoning depth would be wasted on this scope.
